extracted.intended_audience: readers of entertainment news and the comedy/entertainment industry
extracted.subtask_description: A news story reporting the on-stage death of a stand-up comedian, with details about the performance, audience reaction, peers' tributes, and contextual quotes. The piece is aimed at informing general readers and the comedy community about the incident and the comedian's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage presence / liveliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Known for being lively, comedy veteran Cognito...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights that Cognito was 'known for being lively,' implying that energetic stage presence is a notable quality for a stand-up comic. This is presented as part of his reputation and a positive attribute for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement / performative believability
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience thought it was part of his set because it didn’t seem unusual. However, they realized something was wrong when his fellow comedians ran to the stage to help him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers who blur the line between act and reality can make audience reaction unpredictable; believability of the performance can lead audiences to interpret real emergencies as part of the routine. This passage implies that convincing delivery/ambiguity is a feature of some acts but carries risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dark or risky humor
rubrics_metrics.description: An audience member said that Cognito was joking about having a stroke right before he sat down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records Cognito joking about a serious health event as part of his set, indicating that dark, risky, or self-referential jokes about grave subjects are part of his comedic style. This can contribute to shock value and authenticity but may also mask actual emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer health / fitness to perform
rubrics_metrics.description: Andrew Bird, the host for the evening’s show, told BBC that Cognito had been feeling ill before going on stage, but seemed to be better as he started his performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The account notes pre-existing illness before performing; implicitly, a consideration for performers and organizers is assessing a comedian's health before a set. The article presents this as contextual information related to the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage safety and emergency response
rubrics_metrics.description: They realized something was wrong when his fellow comedians ran to the stage to help him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not an explicit guideline, the narrative emphasizes fellow performers and staff responding when a real emergency occurred, implying the importance of on-site awareness and immediate assistance during live shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to craft / 'dying on stage' ethos
rubrics_metrics.description: Atic Bar owner Ryan Mold said that dying on stage is the way Cognito wanted to go adding 'except he’d want more money and a bigger venue'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quote frames dying while performing as an ultimate expression of dedication to comedy, and presents a wry, irreverent industry attitude toward a performer's commitment. It suggests that total dedication to performing (even literally) is celebrated in certain comedy circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional kindness and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Jimmy Carr: 'I’ll never forget his kindness when I started out & how god damn funny he was.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer testimony stressing Cognito's kindness to newcomers is presented as an important professional quality—generosity and mentorship toward less experienced comics is valued and part of a comedian's legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer recognition / reputation among comedians
rubrics_metrics.description: Since his death, his fellow comedians such as Jimmy Carr ... paid tribute to him on Twitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of public tributes from well-known peers is used as evidence of a comedian's impact and standing within the community; positive peer recognition functions as an evaluative indicator of career significance.
